name: Chukwuemeka's Three Seconds (The Null Feed Moment)
creator: Chukwuemeka Osei-Farrell (amateur feed creator, Tier 2); distributed via Frequency Commons
description: In 2219, Tier 2 feed creator Chukwuemeka Osei-Farrell uploaded a three-second neural clip of himself doing nothing — no audio, no haptic signal, no emotional metadata, no visual interest, just the raw feed of sitting in a chair — and titled it 'Here.' The clip spread because it was the only piece of content on any major feed platform that contained genuine zero-stimulus, which BCI users experienced as a startling, almost physical silence in a constant stream of optimized content. Over 4 million people shared it in the first week. Many described crying without knowing why.
cultural_impact: The clip became a landmark in discussions about neural feed saturation and attention economy; it is regularly cited by BCI wellness researchers as evidence of pervasive stimulus exhaustion across the population, and is still shared as a form of digital palate cleansing.
controversy: Multiple corponation feed platforms repeatedly de-amplified the clip using engagement optimization algorithms — because content with zero engagement signals gets suppressed automatically — requiring manual resharing to keep it visible, which became its own secondary story.
story_hooks: Chukwuemeka Osei-Farrell has refused every licensing offer for the clip, including a significant one from a BCI wellness corporation, and no one is entirely sure why.

A researcher studying the clip's neurological effects discovers that a small subset of viewers experienced a specific memory during the three seconds — always the same type of memory — and wants to know why.
Someone has created a fake 'Here 2' clip with subtle embedded haptic content disguised as null-stimulus, and it's circulating alongside the original.
